reviews.author: AJ's studio
reviews.text: First visit in December 2025 | I came to Acorn Garden, where I could feel the Ghibli sensibility. It was a shame that the ivy covering the building had disappeared because it was winter, but the fairytale-like interior with photo spots here and there was very pretty. Although I entered at 9:30 am, there were already quite a few Japanese people, and I was surprised that the staff was also fluent in Japanese. There were many types of bread, including acorn-shaped bread and salt bread, and the large canelé with cute toppings also looked delicious. The Greek yogurt topped with real honeycomb seemed a bit expensive, the coffee was reasonable, and the acorn bread with soft cream inside was highly recommended. The second floor had more seats and there was a table that could seat 6 people. Of course, there is no parking lot, so you have to use a private parking lot nearby.

reviews.text:
The area around Anguk-dong in Gangbuk is where many traditional Hanok-style buildings remain and are gathered together. I heard that this cafe opened a while ago, but I didn't have time to come by, so I had some time while stopping by the city hall, so I decided to go there this time to have a cup of coffee and taste some bread. It is said that this place was a Korean restaurant. Could it be said that such a store took its place in Hanok-style architecture with coffee and bread?
As an architecture major, I didn't really like Hanok before, but recently I started to really like Hanok-style buildings, their interior spaces, and the time I spent relaxing there.
A cafe like this opened up around Anguk Station, and when I came here, I could see foreigners enjoying coffee and bread and spending time, so I felt good without realizing it. I felt like I was a Korean living in a foreign country.
On this day, it rained heavily since morning. Foreign friends who couldn't bring their umbrellas took pictures in front of the pretty building in the rain.
I also enjoyed warm coffee and bread while looking out the window at some friends.
Even though it's raining, the warm Americano is filled with cold rain and the cold wind and rain that comes in through the automatic doors that open as people come and go. The cold wind warmed my body for a moment.
Should I say that the bread is really pretty and neatly displayed?
It's a waste to even eat. A variety of breads that are so pretty.
I chose a few and tried them. It was really soft and delicious.
I often saw them taking a break among the foreigners.
They took pictures and talked at this pretty cafe.
I will move somewhere again. Although this coffee shop with traditional Hanok architecture is small, I think it was enough to provide time for relaxation.
Just like when we go abroad, there are cafes or bakeries we want to visit again.
They too. I guess so.

Jeongsan Sojong Kombucha (+ Mushroom Brown Miskobi Lab)
It was held as a kombucha vin choade, and the history and stories about tea were interesting, and the story about the process of making kombucha was also very interesting.

reviews.author: JEONGHYEON
reviews.text:
The place was smaller than I thought, but the atmosphere and taste were worth giving a thumbs up.
In particular, the white ragu was really delicious even when it cooled down.
The basil pesto was really delicious.
The thick sauce and noodles went well together, and it was by far the best basil food I've ever had!! Tomatoes and pistachios were also a fantastic combination.
The gambasgamberry was delicious, but it was a common flavor that I had tried before, so I was a little disappointed, but it tasted good enough.
I definitely plan to go to try other menu items!!!
However, what is disappointing is that one drink per person is required.
In addition to the wine listed on the menu, you can also order drinks such as carbonated water or apple soda.
It's a restaurant that tastes good and is worth a visit to get in the mood.

The table inside has a very low ledge, but it was dark inside the store so I couldn't see it and almost fell. Seeing as other people almost fell, I think this happens often, but I was a little confused because there was no special warning to be careful. The bathroom is very small. Wonseo-dong 2nd course that is hard to pass up❣️

They are selling a set that comes with the dessert of the day when you choose a drink. There are brown rice coffee, rice flour, and fermented pears, and depending on the type, you cannot choose ice/hot. ☕️

In my case, there were 4 types of desserts: juak, yakgwa, sweet persimmon geotjeori(?), rice cake, and mascarpone cream cheese. All of them were not just sweet, but were more delicious and enjoyable. 😋

You happened to visit on a snowy day and took in the unexpected and overwhelming scenery for a while, right? It was a truly special experience to see the snow-covered Hanok. ❄️

Please refer to this if you are interested in Korean desserts or Hanok view cafes. ❤️

As a content creator, sometimes, not often, I prepare for the experience in advance. Instead of just wandering around and joining the first place that catches my eye, I make reservations in advance for places I know will be interesting.
But sometimes, if you're lucky, you discover places you would never have found through search.

When I arrived at the pizza place I went to for lunch in Ikseon-dong, a sign with a cute bear drawing caught my eye at the corner at the end of a narrow alley. I left my wife and son at the restaurant and went in.
There was a place called Ssamjang, and they were selling bear-shaped shaved ice and shaved ice. It was the perfect place to enjoy dessert with my 7 year old who loves shaved ice (and of course he also likes cute things!). 🥳
So I ordered shaved ice, shaved ice, and two cups of coffee. I paid 34,500 won for dessert, which was much more expensive than lunch... But I still think it's too expensive... especially since no one liked the cake. 😔 I didn't like it because it was cheesecake, but my wife and son also said it wasn't tasty. It didn't taste very good and the texture was strange... so I couldn't eat it all. 😓
I ate the whole cake, but the ratio of ice and toppings wasn't right, so at the end there was only ice and milk left (there was too much milk). 👎
The atmosphere here is somewhere between a cafe and an art gallery. It's elegant but feels cold. The location is really good as it's in the middle of Ikseon-dong, but it's very quiet inside.
Of course, like other places in Seoul, there was no service here.

The pictures were pretty, but the food was really bad... 👎

reviews.text:
After eating bibim cold noodles at Ujuok, I was planning to stop by Mummi, which has delicious original pumpkin pie and lemon pie, but the weather was hot so I decided to stop by Bubing, which looked good and had matcha shaved ice that I saw in Dawn's review last time.

When I arrived in front of Bubing, there didn't seem to be many people waiting, so I tried to wait and eat, but when I saw that there was a queuing system in front of the store, there were over 20 teams waiting, so I thought it would take too long, so I thought about going to Bubing Gahoe branch, which was advertised on the store window.

I didn't have much good experience with stores that appeared on TV, so I hesitated. Still, I thought I'd stop by once, but on my way there, I looked at Manpul and was curious about Sujeonggwa. I saw Socheon, which I had saved in I Want to Go, and there was red bean shaved ice on the menu. I felt uncomfortable that it was a store that appeared on Wednesday Gourmet, so I decided to stop by Socheon and changed my destination.

When I passed through the narrow alley and stood in front of the store, I looked at the sky and saw white clouds floating in the bright blue sky, making me think it was the middle of summer.

In my imagination, it seemed like it would be on the second floor of a building, but it wasn't, and it was located on the first floor. When I entered the store, the only person in the relatively small store was the female manager who was talking on the phone.

I was the only customer in the store, so I sat down at the widest table by the window, which he told me would be great if the red bean shaved ice tasted good. He ended the phone call and brought me a menu. I was curious about Sujeong, but the weather was hot, so I put it off until next time and today I asked for the red bean shaved ice, which is made with self-made red beans.

Inside the store, I could smell the faint smell of a traditional tea house, and the scenery outside the window was so green that it gave off a Korean feel, so my anticipation grew.

I was wondering if they wanted ice, so they put red beans on top of the ice, sprinkled condensed milk, added toppings, etc. and served it with traditional Korean snacks.

At first glance, the visual of the voluminous red bean shaved ice looks simple, perhaps because it is not a red bean shaved ice restaurant. Looking at the toppings, the unit price seems high, but I don't know if cranberries or macadamia nuts would be suitable as toppings for red bean shaved ice.

When I took a spoonful and tasted it, the shaved ice was made with too much raw ice, and the texture was old-fashioned, which is not easy to find these days. The sweetness of the condensed milk sprinkled on top of the red beans was relatively rich, so I laughed because it was an amateurish taste that was far from the classic taste of red bean shaved ice that I tasted at places like Gangjeong Restaurant near my house.

The cranberries that went up as a garnish turned out to be real cranberries when I tasted them, and the macadamia nuts had a hint of sauce, and the macadamia nuts themselves had a buttery taste that didn't go well with the red bean shaved ice. It's good that it used expensive ingredients, but it was still unbalanced, so the amateurish combination was fun.

There is nothing much to say about the traditional Korean sweets since they are common and not from specialty stores such as Imoban, a Byeonggwa store near Sungshin Women's University Station.

Still, after having a refreshing drink, I waited for the lady owner to come out of the store for a while, paid the bill, and then came out.

Overall, the wait time at Bubing, which I was originally planning to stop by, was long, so I was curious about Sujeonggwa instead, so I stopped by Gwicheon first, which I saved because I wanted to go there. The red bean shaved ice I tasted today was somewhere between not so good and okay, but the ample volume and amateurish taste were fun, and I rented out the shop to myself and enjoyed it at my leisure, and it was delicious with the addition of the premium quality of a long-established store.

However, I don't think I'll stop by to eat red bean shaved ice, but I intend to visit again to try Sujeonggwa or traditional tea.

reviews.author: Gustel Gans

Gemütliches Café mit fantastischem Bingsu
Der Eingang ist zwar etwas versteckt, doch innen erwartet einen ein umso gemütliheres Ambiente. Das Personal war ausgesprochen freundlich und half uns bei der Bestellung. Geschmacklich zählt dieses Bingsu zu den besten, die wir je probiert haben – wir hatten Tiramisu und Erdbeere und waren restlos begeistert. Dieses Café können wir wärmstens empfehlen!

Cozy Café with Fantastic Bingsu
The entrance is a little hidden, but inside you’ll find a wonderfully cozy atmosphere. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helped us with our order. In terms of taste, this is some of the best bingsu we’ve ever had—we tried the tiramisu and strawberry flavors and were absolutely delighted. We can warmly recommend this café!

A cozy and fantastic cafe with shaved ice
The entrance is a bit hidden, but once you go inside, a more cozy atmosphere welcomes you. The staff were very friendly and helped me with my order. The taste was the best shaved ice I've ever had. We had the tiramisu and strawberry flavor and were blown away. I really highly recommend this cafe!

This place, which has calm wood tones but makes you feel endlessly excited, is great for looking back on the end of the day and putting an end to it, but it is even more recommended as a space to greet the morning leisurely!

As fall begins, this is a place I want to visit very diligently from this season.

reviews.text:
#Gwanhun-dong #Simwoobang

“A real tea house with a real Korean tea master from Jeju”

There are many good traditional tea houses in Insa-dong, but most of them seem to buy commercially available tea and focus on the atmosphere.
Although it is not well known, Simwoobang can be said to be a 100% handmade traditional tea house that has all the elements that a traditional tea house should have.

The owner of Simwoobang, a traditional beverage craftsman, has been making and serving all the teas in one place for decades.
He is a tea craftsman from Jeju Island and has been interested in food since he was young, and he still maintains that taste to this day.
It is said that a group even came from Japan to learn the owner's tea making skills, so his skills are already recognized.

Schisandra chinensis tea and sujeonggwa are calmly delicious without any artificial sweetness.
The handmade #GingerPyeonggang provided together is also different from the ones sold at department stores, and has a sharp aroma and taste.

Although it was my first visit, I can clearly feel this person's philosophy about food.
He knows how to make the food taste exactly as it should, and he has the skill to do so.
It is the leisure of a craftsman and the skill of a craftsman.

Along with my stomach healing from Manhaenghwa, my mind also became clearer in the deep room.
